newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia grants British Gas offshore permit.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia grants British Gas offshore permit.

text.p: Tunisia on Tuesday granted British Gas an offshore hydrocarbons exploration permit, making it the largest foreign holder of Tunisian oil and gas exploration and production acreage, the company said in a statement.
The Ulysse permit, in the Gulf of Gabes, covers 1,912 square kilometres, bringing British gas total Tunisian acreage to 6,528 kilometres.
British Gas and state-controlled Entreprise Tunisienne d'Activities Petrolieres ETAP each have a 50 percent in the Ulysse permit.

British Gas this year started production at the Miskar gas field which has a capacity of up to 4.5 million cubic metres of gas per day processed in its Hannibal processing plant near the city of Sfax.
The company says Miskar already supplies 80 percent of Tunisia's total daily gas demand.
BG shares with ETAP the oil concessions of Gremda, El Hajeb, Rhemoura and Cercina which contain six oil fields with a combined average daily output of around 6,000 barrels per day.
It also has two other exploration permits: Kerkennah West and Amilcar, which contains the Hasdrubal gas discovery currently under evaluation.

The Ulysse permit agreement was signed on Tuesday in Tunis by Tunisian Industry Minister Slaheddine Bouguerra, ETAP's President and General Manager Moncef Boussen and Colin Friedlander, Technical Director of British Gas Exploration and Production.

"The Ulysse permit includes acreage close to the Miskar gas field, the Ashtart oil field and the Hasdrubal gas discovery... (It) secures for Tunisia a commitment to further evaluate the hydrocarbon potential of a very promising area of the Gulf of Gabes," Friedlander said at the signing ceremony.
